steps.body: You can predict the pattern before dividing: a fraction in lowest terms terminates exactly when its denominator's only prime factors are 2 and/or 5 (since our number system is base ten = 2×5). 1/4 terminates because 4 = 2². 1/3 repeats because 3 is neither a 2 nor a 5.
Follow the exact remainders for 1 ÷ 16 until the decimal either ends or cycles.

widget.prompt: Trace the remainder states for 1/16, then decide whether its decimal terminates or repeats.

choices.label: It terminates at 0.0625
choices.feedback: Correct. The remainder reaches zero after four decimal digits, so 1/16 = 0.0625.

choices.label: It repeats because 16 is large
choices.feedback: Denominator size does not decide the pattern. The remainder reaches zero, so this decimal terminates.

choices.label: It repeats after the digit 5
choices.feedback: A repeated cycle requires a previous nonzero remainder to return. Here the final remainder is zero.

widget.successFeedback: The remainder becomes zero, so 1/16 terminates exactly at 0.0625. Its denominator contains only factors of 2.
widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect at least four remainder states before classifying the decimal.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Continue the exact division until a remainder becomes zero or a previous nonzero remainder repeats.

predict.prompt: In lowest terms, what happens when a fraction's denominator has only factors 2 and 5?

options.label: Its decimal type cannot be predicted

predict.reveal: Every power of 10 is built from factors 2 and 5. A lowest-terms denominator containing only those factors divides some power of 10 exactly, so its decimal ends.

steps.body: Always simplify first! 3/6 looks like it has a factor of 3 in the denominator, but 3/6 = 1/2 — after simplifying, the 3 cancels away and only a 2 remains, so it terminates.

explanationVariants: 12 has a prime factor of 3, which isn't 2 or 5, so 1/12 repeats.
Even though 12 has 2s in it, the leftover factor of 3 forces a repeating decimal.

options.label: Repeat — 12 has a leftover factor of 3
options.feedback: Right — that factor of 3 is neither 2 nor 5, so it repeats.

options.label: Terminate — 12 is even
options.feedback: Being even isn't enough — 12 = 2² × 3, and that 3 forces a repeat.

options.label: Terminate — 12 is a multiple of 4
options.feedback: It has a 4 in it, but also an extra factor of 3, which forces a repeat.

options.label: Can't tell
options.feedback: You can tell — factor 12 = 2² × 3 and check for anything besides 2s and 5s.

options.label: Terminate — 25's only prime factor is 5
options.feedback: Right — 25 = 5², only 5s, so 7/25 terminates.

options.label: Repeat — 25 isn't a power of 2
options.feedback: It doesn't need to be a power of 2 — powers of 5 terminate too, and 25 = 5².

options.label: Repeat — 7 is prime
options.feedback: The NUMERATOR's factors don't matter here — only the denominator's.

options.label: Can't tell without dividing
options.feedback: 25 = 5² — only 5s, so it terminates. No division needed to know that.

explanationVariants: 6 has a leftover factor of 3 after removing the 2, so 5/6 repeats.
2×3 isn't all 2s and 5s — that stray 3 guarantees a repeating decimal.

options.label: Repeat — 6 = 2 × 3, and that 3 isn't allowed
options.feedback: Right — the leftover 3 forces a repeat.

options.label: Terminate — 6 is even
options.feedback: Being even only removes the 2 — the leftover 3 still forces a repeat.

options.label: Terminate — 5 and 6 share no factors
options.feedback: That's true (5/6 is already in lowest terms), but it's the denominator's PRIME factors that decide this, not whether it's simplified.

options.label: Can't tell
options.feedback: 6 = 2 × 3 — the 3 is neither 2 nor 5, so it repeats.

widget.prompt: 3/6 — will it terminate or repeat? (Careful: simplify first!)

options.label: Terminate — 3/6 = 1/2 once simplified
options.feedback: Right — after simplifying, only a 2 remains in the denominator.

options.label: Repeat — 6 = 2 × 3, and 3 isn't allowed
options.feedback: That reasoning applies to 5/6, but 3/6 simplifies to 1/2 FIRST — the 3 cancels away entirely.

options.label: Repeat — any fraction with a 3 somewhere repeats
options.feedback: It's the SIMPLIFIED denominator's prime factors that matter — 3/6 reduces to 1/2, no 3 left.

options.label: Can't tell without dividing
options.feedback: Simplify first: 3/6 = 1/2, and 2 is allowed — it terminates.

explanationVariants: Terminating fractions simplify to denominators built only from 2s and 5s; the rest repeat.
Check each denominator's prime factors after simplifying — only 2s and 5s means it stops.

widget.prompt: Sort each fraction: does it terminate or repeat?
widget.missFeedback: Not quite — check the sorted pile against the denominator's prime factors.
widget.successFeedback: All sorted correctly — 2s and 5s terminate, anything else repeats.

steps.body: The simplify-first trap, one more time.
explanationVariants: 6/15 simplifies to 2/5 first — only a 5 remains, so it terminates.
Don't judge 15 directly; reduce 6/15 by 3 first, leaving denominator 5.

options.label: Terminate — 6/15 = 2/5 once simplified
options.feedback: Right — simplified, only a 5 remains in the denominator.

options.label: Repeat — 15 = 3 × 5, and 3 isn't allowed
options.feedback: That's true of 15 itself, but 6/15 simplifies to 2/5 FIRST, and the 3 cancels away.

options.label: Repeat — the original denominator has a 3
options.feedback: Simplify before judging — 6 and 15 share a factor of 3, and it cancels out entirely.

options.label: Can't tell without dividing
options.feedback: Simplify first: 6/15 = 2/5, and 5 is allowed — it terminates.

hints: Before checking the denominator's prime factors, is 6/15 already in lowest terms?
6 and 15 share a common factor — divide both by it.
6/15 = 2/5 once simplified by 3 — denominator 5, only a 5, so it terminates.

steps.body: The denominator's prime factors — after simplifying — predict the pattern.
takeaways: Only 2s and 5s in the simplified denominator means the decimal terminates.
Any other prime factor (3, 7, 11, …) forces a repeating decimal.
Always simplify the fraction BEFORE checking its denominator.
steps.teaser: Next: turning a repeating decimal back into a fraction.

concept.body: A fraction (in lowest terms) terminates only when its denominator's prime factors are all 2s and/or 5s. Any other prime factor forces a repeat.

explanationVariants: Both prime factors of 10 are allowed, so the division stops cleanly.

options.label: Terminate
options.feedback: Right — 10's only prime factors are 2 and 5.

options.label: Repeat
options.feedback: 10 = 2 × 5 — both are allowed, so it terminates, not repeats.

options.label: Depends on the numerator
options.feedback: Only the denominator's prime factors decide this.

options.label: Can't tell
options.feedback: 10 = 2 × 5, only allowed primes — it terminates.
